subject: distributions badly in need of testing then refactoring

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: distributions badly in need of testing then refactoring
parts:
I've been trying to knock off outstanding Stan math lib
issues and got to this one:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/37

But the tests are seriously lacking, so I don't trust myself
to refactor, so I created this massive project issue as a first step:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/357

What we are really going to need to do is prioritize the functions
and start smaller, one distribution at a time. I just put
that mega-issue in there as a placeholder.

I'm just going to close issue

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/37

because it barely even scratches the surface of what would be found
in even a superficial review of this code.

Any takers? I seriously think this could be a yearlong project
for someone it's in such a dire state right now. If you don't
believe me, just look at some of those files!

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] distributions badly in need of testing then refactoring
parts:
Along the same lines of the issues listed, any distribution which takes a covariance matrix (or uses any sort of linear algebra) should probably be reviewed to confirm that it's using things like LDLT and LLT properly and not refactoring the matrix multiple times.  Even if it only calls mdivide_left_spd once, there should be a test for positive definiteness which should use either LDLT or LLT.

Cheers,
Marcus
